manifest.description: Your cloud accounts, in plain language. See every AWS account Kiro Crew can use with a health light per account and matched reconnect guidance, plus an S3-backed cloud drive — files, a cloud artifact library, and backups — with time-boxed share links. Nothing is public unless you say so, and every paid service asks for your confirmation before it can bill you.
manifest.highlight_1: One health light per account, each with reconnect guidance matched to how the profile authenticates
manifest.highlight_2: Private, encrypted, versioned storage that is created only after you confirm it
manifest.highlight_3: Your cloud artifact library, files, and backups all live on one bucket you own
manifest.highlight_4: Share links always expire — nothing is public unless you say so
manifest.highlight_5: Every paid service is confirmed per account before its first use, and every change is on the record
manifest.use_case_1: See every AWS account Kiro Crew can reach, which ones are healthy, and what this month is costing you -- without opening the AWS console.
manifest.configuration_1: Add an account from the profiles already on this machine, then confirm each paid service once per account before it is first used.

console.backup_restore_caveat: Restore needs read access to the backup folder. The recommended least-privilege policy deliberately grants write only, so it will be denied unless the account's credentials are broader.
console.backup_remote_error: Couldn't read the stored backups just now.
console.backup_restore_failed: Couldn't restore that backup. Nothing was written.
console.backup_restored_note: Your current data was not replaced. The backup was downloaded to a staging folder at the path below.
console.backup_restore_recovered_note: This install's own upload was downloaded and checked against what it recorded. Something else had written over it on the drive, and can do the same to your next upload. Start with the other installs this page lists as backing up to this drive.
console.backup_install_hint: Each install stores its backups under its own name, so a restore can tell this install's archives from another install's.
console.backup_install_rename_failed: Couldn't save the install name. It is unchanged.
console.backup_none_from_this_install: No backups from this install. Include the other installs' archives to see theirs.

console.backup_others_truncated: Only the first {{max}} other installs are shown.
console.backup_archives_truncated: Some {{kind}} archives could not be listed. The newest may be missing.
console.backup_shared_note: One drive shared by two installs is not shared memory and not shared sessions. Each backup is a separate archive of one point in time, and a restore only downloads that file to a staging folder — you replace files yourself, with the gateway stopped.
console.backup_restore_foreign_confirm: This archive was uploaded by another install ({{install}}). Restoring it downloads that install's data, not this install's. Download it anyway?
console.backup_restore_unverified_confirm: This archive is stored under this install's own folder, but this install has no record of uploading it. Anything that can write to the drive can create that folder, so it may not be this install's. Download it anyway?
console.backup_restore_unknown_confirm: This archive was uploaded before installs were named, so which install wrote it is unknown. Download it anyway?
console.backup_restore_overwritten_confirm: This install uploaded this archive, but the drive no longer holds what it uploaded — something else has written over it since. Download it anyway?
console.backup_restore_overwritten_refused: This install uploaded this archive, but the drive no longer holds what it uploaded. To download it anyway, open Stored backups and choose Download it.
console.backup_restore_foreign_refused: That archive belongs to another install. Confirm the restore to download it anyway.
console.access_unchecked: These links were not checked against the drive, so a deleted file is not flagged here.
